rows.title_full: AN ACT EXPANDING THE DEFINITION OF PIRACY, MAKING IT A TRANSNATIONAL CRIME AND INCREASING THE PENALTY FOR QUALIFIED PIRACY, THEREBY AMENDING ARTICLES 122 AND 123 OF THE REVISED PENAL CODE AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Section 1. Article 122 of the Revised Penal Code is hereby amended to read as follows: "ART 122. Piracy in general and mutiny in the high seas or in Philippine waters. - The penalty of reclusion perpetua shall be inflicted upon any person who, on ORFROM the high seas, or in Philippine waters, shall attack or seize a vessel AT SEA OR ANCHORED IN PORT OR A COMMUNITY or, not being a member of its complement nor a passenger, shall seize the whole or part of the cargo of said vessel, its equipment,or personal belongings of its complement or passengers.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04624

rows.author: D058
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING AN OPTIONAL RESERVED OFFICERS' TRAINING CORPS (ROTC) PROGRAM FOR ALL EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: In preparing selected students for commissioned service in any regular branch of the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) pursuant to law, all existing Reserved Officers' Training Corps (ROTC) programs, organized into one or more units at any educational institution authorized to grant baccalaureate degrees, shall be optional for all college students. ROTC units in colleges and universities shall continue with ROTC training in accordance with this Act.
rows.status: Substituted by HB03593

rows.author: C093
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2003-06-02, transmitted to on 2003-06-04 and received by the Senate on 2003-06-05
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTING POLICIES GOVERNING THE HOUSEHOLD EMPLOYMENT INDUSTRY, ESTABLISHING A STANDARD OF PROTECTION AND PROMOTING THE WELFARE OF HOUSEHOLD HELPERS AND THEIR FAMILIES
rows.abstract: "Batas Kasambahay." Rationale: Household helpers have been relegated by law, custom and convention to the informal sector of the labor force. They have been deliberately excluded from several protective provisions of law relating to basic rights andprivileges otherwise accorded traditional groups of the labor sector. Since the interaction between employer and household helper is confined within the walls of private residences, the predominantly female members of the industry are unduly exposedto physical, mental and sexual abuse and exploitation. Compounding the problem is the inherent timidity and passiveness of the household helpers themselves, who have little or no awareness of their basic rights and privileges.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05804

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROMOTING A SMOKE-FREE ENVIRONMENT BY REGULATING THE PRODUCTION, MANUFACTURE, LABELING, ADVERTISEMENT AND SALE OF TOBACCO PRODUCTS, AND ESTABLISHING A TRUST FUND THEREOF
rows.abstract: Rationale:  It is the Policy of the State to protect the populace from hazardous products, which is essential for the enjoyment by all the people of the blessing of democracy. The government shall promote a smoke-free environment with the penultimate objective of regulating tobacco products inasmuch as these products remain to be the major threat to people's health and to the environment.

rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING REPRESENTATION OF CONSUMER GROUP IN THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF THE MANILA ELECTRIC COMPANY, THE NATIONAL POWER CORPORATION, THE METROPOLITAN WATER SEWERAGE AUTHORITY, THE PHILIPPINE LONG DISTANCE TELEPHONE COMPANY, AND ANY OTHER CORPORATION, GOVERNMENT OR PRIVATE, DISPENSING PUBLIC SERVICES, GIVING THEM ONE (1) SEAT IN THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to grant REPRESENTATION of the CONSUMERS in the Board of Directors of the Manila Electric Company, the Nationa Power Corporation, the Metropolitan Water Sewerage Authority, The Philippine Long Distance Telephone Company, and any other corporation, government or private, dispensing public services like the one mentioned, giving them one (1) seat in the Board of Directors of these corporations.

rows.author: C137
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A MAGNA CARTA OF STUDENTS
rows.abstract: This bill aims to promote further the students' rights and welfare and to enhance their role and potentials towards social change and development. Among other fundamental rights of the students already enshrined in the Constitution, the Magna Cartaof Students guarantees the students' right to be represented in policy-making bodies of the school, to govern its own activities, to discipline its own rank and be accorded due process in disciplinary proceedings. Moreover, the bill provides for penalties to any person who shall willfully interfere with, restrain or coerce any student in the exercise of his or her right guaranteed under this Act.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C137
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING GREEN CARDS HOLDERS FROM BEING APPOINTED TO ANY PUBLIC OFFICE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NUMBERED EIGHT HUNDRED SEVEN, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE CIVIL SERVICE DECREE OF THE PHILIPPINES (pd 807)
rows.abstract: NO GREEN CARD HOLDERS SHALL BE ELIGIBLE FOR APPOINTMENT TO ANY OFFICE IN THE GOVERNMENT, OR IN ANY GOVERNMENT OWNED OR CONTROLLED CORPORATION, UNLESS IT IS SHOWN BY CLEAR EVIDENCE THAT He/she MADE AN IRREVOCABLE WAIVER OF THAT STATUS OR THAT HE HASSURRENDERED HIS GREEN CARD TO THE APPROPRIATE U.S. AUTHORITIES.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C137
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTING A COMPREHENSIVE `KAUNLARAN NG KABATAAN AT MAMAMAYAN DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM' TO PROMOTE THE PHYSICAL, INTELLECTUAL AND SOCIAL WELL-BEING OF YOUNG PEOPLE AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREOF
rows.abstract: The bill proposes to establish a comprehensive Youth Development Program.  It seeks to promote the involvement of the youth in the character building and development activities for a civic efficiency, self-improvemen t and economic well-being. The programs are composed of various components such as: sports development, scholarship, livelihood training and cooperative organization. These areas of development will provide our youth the necessary opportunities to discover their social and economicpotentials to become self-reliant, productive and responsible citizens of the country.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on YOUTH AND SPORTS DEVELOPMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO GRANT MONTHLY PENSION TO GOVERNMENT RETIREES UNDER REPUBLIC ACT NO. 1616 WHO HAVE REACHED THE AGE OF SEVENTY-FOUR (74), APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale:  In A survey conducted of retirees who opted to retire under Republic Act No. 1616 revealed that a majority of this class of retirees have been living in abject poverty, and many of them have to depend on doleouts from close relatives andfriends.  Aged government personnel who retired need monthly pension because at their late age their opportunities of earning is already almost nil.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING DIFFICULTY DIFFERENTIAL TO GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: This proposal for a difficulty differential seeks to encourage government workers to go where they are most needed. In return for additional incentives, it is hoped that qualified teachers, doctors, nurses and other government functionaries would be more visible in the underserved countryside. At the same time, this bill seeks to reward the pioneering few who comtinue to labor in far-flung and difficult-to-re ach communities, unmindful of the dangers and hardship that go with workingwith less-privileged Filipinos.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT LOWERING THE RETIREMENT AGE OF GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED EIGHTY-TWO HUNDRED AND NINETY-ONE, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE REVISED GSIS ACT OF 1997
rows.abstract: This bill REDUCES the age for compulsory retirement to SIXTY (60), and for optional retirement to FIFTY-FIVE (55) years of age.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 13-A OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8291 (GSIS ACT OF 1997) BY PRESCRIBING OTHER CONDITIONS FOR ENTITLEMENT TO THE RETIREMENT BENEFITS, UNDER SECTION 13 OF THE SAME ACT, FOR GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEE OR OFFICIAL WHO RETIRES OR HAS PREVIOUSLYRETIRED AS A RESULT OF BEING PHASED OUT AND/OR NOT RETAINED BY HIS OFFICE/BUREAU/ CORPORATION PRIVATIZING ABOLISHING HIS OFFICE
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to AUGMENT the pension benefits of government retirees.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO INTEGRATE A COMPUTER EDUCATION PROGRAM INTO THE EDUCATIONAL SYSTEM AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: In our country's stride to regain lost economic grounds, our people need to be attuned to the latest developments in science and technology. The Filipino youth must be scientifically and technically prepared so that their innate talents may be fullyharnessed for national development. The proposed bill is one way of promoting scientific and technical literacy among the Filipino youth in the field of computer education.
rows.status: Substituted by HR01097

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZ ING THE SCIENTIFIC CAREER SYSTEM
rows.abstract: Rationale: The Scientific Career System (SCS) a system of recruitment, career progression, recognition and reward of scientists and engineers in the public service as a means of developing a pool of highly qualified and productive scientific personnel. This proposal seeks to ensure continued attraction and retention of scientific manpower in research and development, and to reward qualified scientists and technologists.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING FIVE HUNDRED PESOS (P500.00) MONTHLY ALLOWANCE TO ALL BARANGAY TANODS AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale:  As the basic political unit, the barangay has lots of requirements which only bigger political units can provide.  One such need is to provide incentives to those who normally deliver the services in the barangay hierarchy - the barangaytanods.  This bill proposes to grant a standard monthly allowance of FIVE HUNDRED (P500.00) PESOS to all barangay tanods.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING INCENTIVES TO PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS WHO ARE ASSIGNED OUTSIDE OF THEIR TOWNS AND PROVINCES, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Any public school teacher who is assigned to a town other than his own, shall in addition to his basic salary and benefits under the Salary Standardization Law, be entitled to One Thousand (P1,000.00) Pesos monthly as incentive allowance.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZ ING EARLY CHILDHOOD DEVELOPMENT AND EDUCATION CENTERS FOR CHILDREN AGED ZERO TO FIVE, CREATING THE IMPLEMENTING MACHINERY THEREOF, PROVIDING GUIDELINES, INCENTIVES, GOVERNMENT FINANCIAL SUPPORT AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The Centers shall develop a program of activities that will focus primarily on the children's total development according to their individual stages of development, with the child's first language as the medium of instruction. They shall also provide the parents with training programs which shall endeavor to include responsible parenthood, as well provide guidance in child rearing, health, nutrition and education.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A NATIONAL STRATEGIC MISSING CHILDREN RECOVERY PROGRAM, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The program is aimed at developing effective models of national and local coordination and cooperation in locating missing children, effective methods designed to promote community awareness of the problem, and effective programs that provide counseling and treatment to the recovered children and their families.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SOCIAL SERVICES since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE IMPORTATION OF SECOND-HAND OR USED APPLIANCES AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract: Rationale: The importation of the second-hand or used appliances in particular, floods the local market with expensive but defective goods or its durability or quality has greatly diminished. Yet, local consumers prefer these imported goods over thelocal manufactured appliances because of the orientation among many Filipinos that "Anything that is foreign is superior." Consequently, the importation of used appliances gives rise to unfair competition with domestic manufacturers.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT REVERTING TO THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT THE DISCHARGE OF BASIC AGRICULTURAL FUNCTIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIE S DEVOLVED TO LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS AND AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: Rationale: The recent passage of Republic Act No. 8435, otherwise known as the Agriculture Modernization Act of 1997, makes it imperative that the Department of Agriculture, the lead department tasked to implement the law, for its monitoring and data gathering requirements, shall have complete administrative control and supervision over all personnel in the field level that are involved in agriculture and fishery, in order that all effectively implement and achieve the objectives of the Agriculture and Fishery Law.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE NATIONAL ARCHIVES OF THE PHILIPPINES, DEFINING ITS POWERS, FUNCTIONS AND DUTIES, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The establishment of the National Archives of the Philippines will promote sound and efficient records management practices towards the enrichment of archival documents; make archives available for public access and use in accorfdance with the policies of the government; provide centralized and cost-effective repository facilities for the storage and retrieval of semi-active records of public offices, etc.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT REORGANIZATION since 2001-07-24

first_reading.comm_act: chnge of ctte. ref'l from Basic ed &Culture and Approp. as per J.77;p.55( 6-2-5-03)

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING DISCRIMINATION AGAINST FILIPINO EMPLOYEES AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF                         p
rows.abstract: Rationale: This unfair treatment directed at Filipino teachers at the International School is discrimination of the reverse kind. It is directed by foreigners against Filipinos on Philippine soil - a sad legacy of a colonial past still being perpetuated by former colonialists. Under the norms of present day civilization, there is NO superior or dominant race of people, there is NO preferred or rimary class of citizens. To give different compensation based not on merit or seniority or experiencebut solely on race and nationality is illegal, oppressive and unjust.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2001-07-24

principal_referral.committee: MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISE DEVELOPMENT

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE CONSTRUCTION OF PUBLIC RESTROOMS ALONG NATIONAL HIGHWAYS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Land Transport Facilities for Hygiene and Convenience Act."  Public restrooms shall be constructed within a reasonable distance from each other along national highwways. They shall be erected within a distance of at least three (3) meters from theshoulder of the highway, zoning ordinances provision to the contrary notwithstanding .
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC WORKS AND HIGHWAYS since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING THE PRACTICE OF PLUMBING ENGINEERING IN THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Some forty years ago, 1955, Congress enacted R.A. 1378, otherwise known as the Plumbing Law, which regulates the trade of master plumbers. High School graduates with five years plumbing experience used to dominate the trade.  With the advent of high-rise buildings, theirs numbers are dwindling but sustaining. Master plumbers with engineering expertise are coming about. Since then, the law has become outmoded with provisions that do not harmonize with the times.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE REGISTRATION OF VETERINARY DIAGNOSTIC LABORATORY WITH THE BUREAU OF ANIMAL INDUSTRY, PROVIDING FOR THE QUALIFICATIONS OF MANAGERS AND SUPERVISORS THEREOF AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The proprietors of existing livestock and poultry enterprises are now aware of the value and necessity of rapid and accurate diagnostic tests as tools in forestalling bigger losses during outbreaks of diseases in their farms. Accordingly,there is now a great need for veterinary diagnostic services.  At present, government facilities and resources cannot cope up with the increasing demands. Hence, certain individuals have set up diagnostic purposes. Even individuals, knowledgeable about laboratory diagnosis but not own any livestock farm, have put up such diagnostic laboratories to meet the needs of the industry.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE, FOOD & FISHERIES since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: "THE REVISED VETERINARY MEDICINE AND SURGERY ACT"
rows.abstract: Rationale: The importance of animals to man makes imperative the regulation of the profession of those entrusted to manage the country's animal health, to protect man from animal diseases and ensure public nutrition through increased animal production. The protection of public health requires the assurance that veterinarians dedicate their attention to health services.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06002

first_reading.comm_act: change of cttee. ref'l from Health as per J.37; p.20

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING AND VESTING THE BUREAU OF FOOD AND DRUGS WITH QUASI-JUDICIAL POWERS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES, AMENDING CERTAIN SECTIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED THIRTY-SEVEN HUNDRED AND TWENTY, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE "FOODS, DRUGS AND DEVICES, AND COSMETICS ACT"
rows.abstract: Rationale: The Law (RA 3720) which created the Food and Drugs Administration (FDA), as amended by RA 7394 (Consumer Act of the Philippines), failed to clothe the Bureau with the power or authority to administer the law and the rules and regulationsissued pursuant thereto effectively. The existing laws further failed to clarify the extent of the Bureau's regulatory powers making it hesitant and therefore ineffective to implement existing rules and regulations perceived to be beyond the Agency'srule-making authority.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE FILIPINO ACADEMY OF ARTS AND LETTERS, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The Constitution provides that the State shall foster the preservation, enrichment and dynamic evolution of a Filipino national culture based on the principle of unity and diversity in a climate of free artistic and intellectual expression. Arts and letters shall enjoy the patronage of the State, and the State shall conserve, promote and popularize the nation's historical and cultural heritage and resources, as well as, artistic creations. The State shall encourage and support researches and studies on the arts and culture. Pursuant to these constitutional provisions, it is the policy of the Act to provide meaningful incentives to those engaged in arts and letters, give due recognition to outstanding achievements in the same fieeld, and organize the country's artists and writers into a community, receiving State support but free from government interference in managing its own affairs.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT REORGANIZATION since 2001-07-24

first_reading.comm_act: chnge of ctte. refl from Basic Ed & Approp. as per J.77;p.55( 6-2-5-03)

rows.author: B016
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING ADDITIONAL RETIREMENT BENEFITS TO MEMBERS OF THE JUDICIARY, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 910, AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale:  It is of common knowledge that the remuneration accorded to the Justices of the Supreme Court and Court of Appeals and other members of the Judiciary is indecently low.  In response to the call of duty in the administration of justice, most of thwm have had to forego lucrative opportunities elsewhere; yet, after having made a noble sacrifice and having devoted to the best years of their lives to public service, they are not afforded appreciable security after retirement. The existing retirement laws, foremost of which is Republic Act No. 910, as amended, are unresponsive to the rapidly changing economic conditions. The gratuity provided thereunder is not commensurate with the valuable service rendered by the Justices of the Suppreme Court, Court of Appeals and the other members of the Judiciary.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE REHABILITATION AND IMPROVEMENT OF ALL IRRIGATION FACILITIES THROUGHOUT THE COUNTRY, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SIXTY-NINE HUNDRED AND SEVENTY-EIGHT, ENTITLED `AN ACT TO PROMOTE RURAL DEVELOPMENT BY PROVIDING FOR AN ACCELERATED PROGRAM WITHIN A TEN(10)-YEAR PERIOD FOR THE CONSTRUCTION OF IRRIGATION PROJECTS'
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to reemphasize government's commitment to its responsibility in implementing programs that will encourage and motivate farmers to increase agricultural production.  A way to achieve this is by providing an efficient and modernized irrigation system facilities throughout the country.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE, FOOD & FISHERIES since 2001-07-24

rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2002-11-29, transmitted to on 2002-12-02 and received by the Senate on 2002-12-04
rows.title_full: AN ACT EXEMPTING ALL COOPERATIVES FROM ALL TAXES, LEVIES, DUTIES, FEES AND OTHER CHARGES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SIXTY-NINE HUNDRED AND THIRTY-EIGHT, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE COOPERATIVE CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Since the objective of cooperatives is to provide maximum service to its members, they must not be burdened by payments of so many taxex, levies, duties and other fees. In view of the foregoing, approval of this bill is highly recommended.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05206

rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZ ING THE RICE RESEARCH PROGRAM AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale: Our country is presently suffering from acute rice shortage. The government has to import rice from other countries when the Philippines is supposed to be an agricultural country. It is to be noted also that the farmers are maong the poorest of the poor in this country. > To solve these problems, there is a need for intensified research efforts that would balance the increased yield with sustainable production, and using a system that is environmentally safe.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE, FOOD & FISHERIES since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT FURTHER AMENDING SECTIONS 10 AND 65 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6657, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE COMPREHENSIVE AGRARIAN REFORM LAW (CARL), AS AMENDED BY SECTIONS 2 AND 5 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7881, AND THE DECISION OF THE SUPREME COURT IN THE LUZ FARM CASEIMPOSING APPLICATION FEES ON THE EXEMPTION AND CONVERSION OF AGRICULTURAL LANDS TO NON-AGRICULTURA L USES
rows.abstract: In response to the budgetary constraints of the government and to support the realization of a successful agrarian reform program envisioned to enhance agricultural productivity and spur country side development, APPLICATION FEES for exemption and conversion are necessary to raise revenues that will support and complement the CARP.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRARIAN REFORM since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE COLLECTION OF ALL RECORDS AND DOCUMENTS IN ALL GOVERNMENT OFFICES AND PRIVATE COLLECTIONS WHICH MAY HAVE A BEARING ON THE ASSASSINATION OF FORMER SENATOR BENIGNO AQUINO, JR. AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: It is the policy of the State to collage and preserve all historical records and documents, pertaining to the martyrdom of the late Sen. Benigno Aquino, Jr., in line with the principle of government transparency and the right of the people to know.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 13 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 3019, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE `ANTI-GRAFT AND CORRUPT PRACTICES ACT'
rows.abstract: Rationale: The main objective of preventive suspension is to prevent an accused official from interfering with the normal course of his investigation by wielding his influence and authority over the conduct of possible witnesses. Preventive suspension is also said to decrease possible instances of tampering or destruction of evidentiary records by someone still in authority.> Instead of utilizing the wisdom behind the remedy, preventive suspension has unwittingly become the tool for polical reprisals and other base motives.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 24 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6770, OTHERWISE KNOW AS `THE OMBUDSMAN ACT OF 1989'
rows.abstract: Rationale: As a general rule, there is nothing improper in suspending an officer pending his investigation. But there is something wrong when the power to suspend becomes a tool of oppression. This power is most apparent in Section 24 of Republic Act No. 6770 which part provides: "The preventive suspension shall continue until the case is terminated by the Office of the Ombudsman but not more than six months without pay."
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PROMOTE RURAL HEALTH BY PROVIDING FOR AN ACCELERATED PROGRAM FOR THE CONSTRUCTION OF A POTABLE WATER SUPPLY SYSTEM IN EVERY BARANGAY IN THE COUNTRY WITHIN THREE (3) YEARS
rows.abstract: The objective of this bill is to develop a three-year program for the ocnstruction of a potable water supply system in every barangay throughout the country. The provision of a clean water supply source in rural areas in important is order to prevent the outbreak of cholera and other water-borne diseases.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT CONVERTING THE DON JESUS GONZALES HIGH SCHOOL AT THE PANDACAQUI RESETTLEMENT SITE IN BARANGAY PANDACAQUI, MUNICIPALITY OF MEXICO, PROVINCE OF PAMPANGA TO A NATIONAL HIGH SCHOOL, TO BE KNOWN AS THE DON JESUS GONZALES NATIONAL HIGH SCHOOL AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.status: Substituted by HB06202

rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING FARMERS, FISHERMAN AND ENTERPRISES WITH CAPITALIZATION NOT EXCEEDING FIVE HUNDRED THOUSAND PESOS (P500,000.00) MORE ACCESS TO CREDIT FACILITIES, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE CERTAIN PROVISIONS UNDER PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 717, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE AGRI-AGRA LAW AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: An amendment is necessary to redirect the Agri-Agra fund's use in favor of small farmers who, due to lack of capitalization, are left out because of the high credit risk. Left hanging without sufficient capitalization, the small farmer orfishermen is prone to low agricultural production. The amendment will MAXIMIZE the use of the Agri-Agra fund for the benefit of small farmers, fishermen and agricultural enterprise with less than five hundred thousand pesos capitalization.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECONOMIC AFFAIRS since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING GOVERNMENT AGENCIES, SUBDIVISIONS, INSTRUMENTALITI ES AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS TO POST IN CONSPICUOUS PLACES NOTICES INFORMING THE PUBLIC OF FEES AND CHARGES THEY ARE MANDATED TO COLLECT
rows.abstract: Rationale: Section 7 of the Bill of Rights guarantees the people's right to information on matters of public concern and access to records pertaining to official transactions of the government.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2002-05-23, transmitted to on 2002-05-28 and received by the Senate on 2002-05-28
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLE 177 OF EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 209, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE FAMILY CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: Article 177 of the Family Code of the Philippines is hereby amended to read as follows: Only children conceived and born outside of wedlock of parents who, at the time of conception of the former, were not disqualified by any impediment to marry each other may be legitimated. > PROVIDED THAT THOSE CONCEIVED AND BORN TO PARENTS UNDER THE AGE OF MAJORITY (BELOW 18 YEARS OF AGE) MAY BE ELIGIBLE FOR LEGITIMATION BY THE SUBSEQUENT MARRIAGE OF THE PARENTS TO EACH OTHER.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04538

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING THE QUALIFICATIONS OF MEMBERS OF THE PROSECUTION STAFF UNDER THE CHIEF STATE PROSECUTOR AND ASSISTANT CHIEF STATE PROSECUTORS
rows.abstract: Rationale: There are just too many criminal cases filed and too few prosecutors to handle these cases. The pressure of resolving the endless number of cases is further aggravated by the imposition of deadlines. A clogged criminal docket and an impending deadline are consequently irresistible ingredients for a miscarriage of justice. I submit that an effective way of preventing such miscarriage of justice is by simply filling the depleted ranks with more prosecutors. > It is thus submitted thatthis nationwide problem of a depleted prosecutor-forc e can now be remedied by DECREASING the present five-year-actua l-practice requirement to three years.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-07-24

rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2003-10-13, transmitted to on 2003-10-14 and received by the Senate on 2003-10-22
rows.title_full: AN ACT CONVERTING THE PAMPANGA HIGH SCHOOL IN THE CITY OF SAN FERNANDO, PROVINCE OF PAMPANGA TO A NATIONAL HIGH SCHOOL, TO BE KNOWN AS THE PAMPANGA NATIONAL HIGH SCHOOL AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.status: Substituted by HB06220

rows.title_full: AN ACT REORGANIZING THE FERTILIZER AND PESTICIDE AUTHORITY AND EXPANDING ITS POWERS AND DUTIES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NUMBERED ONE THOUSAND ONE HUNDRED AND FORTY-FOUR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill also attempts at establishing a special trust fund for the development of the industry - specifically to subsidize, during emergencies, the purchase of such fertilizers and pesticides needed by the farmers, as well as to serve as an investment fund for the full development and integration of the industry from top to bottom, with the farmers, in the end, overseeing their own progress through the judicious management and utilization of this initial resource base.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1759, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS `AN ACT PENALIZING CONTRACTORS AND SUB-CONTRACTORS WHO VIOLATE ANY MATERIAL PROVISIONS OF CONTRACTS INVOLVING PUBLIC WORKS PROJECTS' BY NOW REQUIRING CONTRACTORS AND SUB-CONTRACTORS TOPOST A BOND WITH THE DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC WORKS AND HIGHWAYS (DPWH) TO ANSWER FOR DAMAGES TO THIRD PERSONS
rows.abstract: Rationale: It has been observed that many public works projects, undertaken by private contractors, are being constructed below specifications, as to materials, quality and quantity of work, in violation of substantial provisions and requirements ofthe contract. Government has suffered tremendous losses, in terms of properties and lives, as a result of these anomalies. There have been numerous cases of buildings collapsing, which have claimed lives. Furthermore, the material claims of victimsare delayed because of the difficulty of collecting from those accountable. Thus, the need for private contractors undertaking public works projects to POST A CASH BOND in order to expedite the claims for damages of third persons due to negligence.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC WORKS AND HIGHWAYS since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLE 1691 OF THE CIVIL CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES AND ARTICLE 147 OF THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: If the house helper is under the age of eighteen years and is qualified for SECONDARY EDUCATION UNDER EXISTING RULES AND REGULATIONS OF THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION, CULTURE AND SPORTS, the head of the family, IN KEEPING WITH THE FINANCIAL CAPACITY OF THE FAMILY, shall give an opportunity to the house helper for at least SECONDARY EDUCATION. The cost of such education shall NOT be a part of the house helper's compensation, unless there is a stipulation to the contrary.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING THE RIGHTS OF PATIENTS AND PRESCRIBING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF
rows.abstract: "Magna Carta of Patient's Rights." Rationale: The Philippine Constitution, in Section 1, Article XIII, states that the Congress shall give the highest priority to the enactment of measures that protect and enhance the right of all people to human dignity. Towards this end, it is hereby declared the policy of the State to ensure and protect the rights of patients to decent, humane and quality health care.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTIONS 51 AND 52, BOOK OF EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 292, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE ADMINISTRATIVE CODE OF 1987
rows.abstract: Rationale: To prevent the scenario of a government official who is unable to fulfill his duties for long and almost indefinite periods of time, it is hereby proposed that Section 51 and 52, Book V of the Administrative Code of 1987 be amended to LIMIT the scope of preventive suspension to a maximum and unqualified period of sixty days upon the issuance of such suspension by the discplining authority.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2001-07-24

rows.abstract: Rationale: Early detection through microscopy is crucial to the control of diseases. In a country such as ours, where the morbidity is high and widespread, particularly in the rural areas, provisions for basic health facilities on early health intervention become as necessary as the tools of production that help sustain life.

rows.abstract: All government-owne d and-controlled corporations and agencies are required to assign at least twenty-five percent (25%) of their advertising expenditures to advertise in the regional, pronvincial, municipal, city publications and ratio stations.

rows.abstract: All mail matter of private citizens addressed to the Committee on Constitutional Amendments of the Senate and the House of Representatives shall be received, transmitted and delivered in the mail free of postage; provided that the mail matter shallbe sent by ordinary mail only, and provided further that said mail matter shall be addressed to the Committee on Constitutional Amendments or either the Senate or the House of Representatives .

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING MINI-FOREST RESERVES FOR EVERY MUNICIPALITY
rows.abstract: "2001 Act of Compulsory Mini-Forest Reserves for Municipalities. " Rationale: Rapid deforestation being a national concern, cannot be adequately addressed by the Administrative agencies alone. Any serious success in addressing this concern would necessarily include the indispensable support of local governments. The proposed bill seeks to complement the DENR-led reforestation projects by galvanizing the nationwide efforts of municipal local governments. In creating together small but permanentmini-forest reserves, this alliance of efforts may bear fruit and better address the problem at hand.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05812

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 318, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE CHEMICAL ENGINEERING LAW OF THE PHILIPPINES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The bill basically addresses the need to revise Republic Act 318, otherwise known as the Chemical Engineering Law and seeks to make it a policy of the State to promote the development of the chemical engineering profession as a vital input to national development.
rows.status: Substituted by HB00046

rows.abstract: Rationale: Republic Act No. 877 or the Philippine Nursing Law was approved in 1953. Its amendatory act, R.A. 4704, was approved IN June 1966. Since then, there has been no amendatory decrees, act or executive order, besides the Professional Regulations Act, which affected and regulated the nursing profession in line with the constitutional mandate for government to regulate and supervise the profession in the country.

rows.abstract: It is the policy of the State to give the Filipino youth, particularly in remote areas, the chance for upward mobility through education not only by listening but also reading. Towards this end, all public schools and libraries in remote barangays shall be provided with books under the Books for the Barrios Program.

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTIONS 285 AND 286 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991, PROVIDING FOR AN EQUITABLE DISTRIBUTION OF THE INTERNAL REVENUE ALLOTMENT (IRA) TO LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to CORRECT the INEQUITY in distributing the IRA to LGUs by introducing poverty-sensiti ve factors in the IRA formula in lieu of population, land area and equal sharing. These are: population density, poverty incidence and the incomeclass of LGUs. Studies show that these factors, if used to calculate for IRA shares of LGUs, would favor poorer provinces, cities, muicipalities ad barangays.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D040
rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING AS PRIMA FACIE EVIDENCE OF GRAFT AND CORRUPTION, INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS BELOW THE PRESCRIBED STANDARDS OR SPECIFICATIONS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED THIRTY HUNDRED NINETEEN (REPUBLIC ACT NO. 3019), OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE ANTI-GRAFT AND CORRUPT PRACTICES ACT
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to declare as prima facie evidence of graft and corruption substandard infrastructures in order to discourage officials of the government, contractors and other people involved from the utter misuse of government funds.

rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE RATE OF BASE PAY OF OFFICERS AND ENLISTED PERSONNEL OF THE ARMED FORCES OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to increase the base pay of officers and enlisted personnel of the Armed Forces of the Philippines to be at par with the rate of pay of members of the PNP of equivalent rank.  This proposed increase in pay will definitely go a long way in improving the living condition of military personnel and thus enhance professionalism in the AFP.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING RETIREMENT, DEATH, DISABILITY AND OTHER BENEFITS FOR THE PROSECUTORS AND THE LEGAL STAFF OF THE DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: This Act shall apply to all members of the National Prosecution Service which include all state prosecutors, provincial and city prosecutors and their assistants, and members of the legal staff or the state counsel of the Department of Justice, regardless of their employment status.

rows.author: B016
rows.title_full: AN ACT MAKING ROAD RAGE AGGRAVATING CIRCUMSTANCE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE REVISED PENAL CODE, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: ROAD RAGE IS DEFINED AS THE VIOLENT OR AGGRESSIVE BEHAVIOR OF A MOTORIST ON THE ROAD DIRECTED AGAINST AND IS A REACTION TO ACTS OF OTHER MOTORISTS PERCEIVED BY THE FIRST MOTORIST AS INSULTS OR ONE-UP-MANSHIP, GIVING RISE TO AN ALTERCATION WHICH RESULTS IN DEATH, INJURY AND/OR DAMAGE TO PROPERTY OF THE SECOND MOTORIST, OTHER MOTORISTS OR THIRD PARTIES.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B016
rows.title_full: AN ACT LIMITING THE AUTHORITY OF THE DEPUTY OMBUDSMAN FOR THE ARMED FORCES TO THE INVESTIGATION AND PROSECUTION OF COMPLAINTS AGAINST UNIFORMED MEMBERS OF THE ARMED FORCES OF THE PHILIPPINES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6770, OTHERWISEKNOWN AS "THE OMBUDSMAN ACT OF 1989"
rows.abstract: Rationale: This bill seeks to limit the authority of the Deputy Ombudsman for the Armed Forces to investigate and prosecute uniformed members of the Armed Forces of the Philippines. > The military organization is peculiar. It has its own customs, traditions, practices, and code of conduct. It is clothed  with the responsibility of security the state. All these set it apart from the ordinary civilian life.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B016
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING PHILIPPINE EMBASSIES AND CONSULATES TO CONDUCT CLASSES FOR CHILDREN OF FILIPINOS IN OTHER COUNTRIES, TO EDUCATE THEM ON PHILIPPINE HISTORY, CULTURE, LANGUAGES AND CIVICS AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: All Philippine embassies and Consulates, particularly in countries where there are many Filipino expatriates, are hereby required to conduct special classes, free of charge, during Saturdays for the children of Filipino parentage, to educate them onPhilippine history, languages, culture and civics.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on FOREIGN AFFAIRS since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B016
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE PHILIPPINE COFFEE AND TROPICAL FRUITS DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale: The creation of a national coffee and tropical fruits development authority is aimed at increasing the productivity of the coffee and tropical fruit trees and improving the quality of its fruits. It is also hoped that in the process, theutility of the trees will be maximized. The approval of this bill will not only improve the country's coffee and tropical fruit industry but will also promote national development and progress.
